messages:
Alex K.: Thinking about a small Console change — can we surface a per-route 'visible sampling breakdown' (sample rate + redaction level + last-decision-reason) so SREs and customers can see why certain requests were kept unredacted for audits?
Priya M.: Curious — is this just telemetry (aggregates) or do you mean links to the actual sampled events? we need to avoid exposing PII in the UI. :thinking_face:
Jamal R.: The ask from security was: show the sampling rationale and a count of unredacted events, plus a way to request a time-bounded, auditable export (breakglass) if compliance needs raw logs. Not raw data in the console itself.
Sasha T.: Important: any link to a raw export must require a separate approval flow (audit ticket + 2FA). Otherwise we violate retention/consent rules. Also need to log who requested and why.
Alex K.: Proposal: Console shows per-route row: `sample_rate`, `redaction_policy` (enum: hash/anonymize/none), `last_changed_by`, `last_change_ts`, and a small explainers popover. For exports, a modal that creates an ephemeral export token (TTL=12h) after approval.
Priya M.: That sounds ok. On redaction_policy: add `consent_required` flag per-route. If consent_required=true, exports are blocked unless opt-in flag present for those customers. Also need to store a hashed user id for reconciling without exposing raw PII.
Jamal R.: For the ephemeral export flow: backend issues an `export_request` record with status {pending, approved, rejected}. OpsBot: deploy-notify: export-service v2 rolled to canary on prod 3.
Sasha T.: UX detail: show last 30d sampled counts, but don't show sample examples inline. Instead show anonymized examples (redacted and tokenized) if someone clicks "peek" and has permission. Example anonymized snippet: `{"prompt":"[REDACTED_EMAIL] asked about billing","response":"[REDACTED_PERSON] OK"}`
Alex K.: Implementation sketch (config snippet):
```
routes:
  - id: "embed-prod-1"
    sampling:
      rate: 0.01
      redaction: "hash"
      consent_required: true
    exports:
      allowed: false
```
Priya M.: We should define allowed redaction modes mapping to actual tokenization functions in the runtime and list them in the console help. Also add a guard: if `redaction=none` and `rate>0.001` require an enterprise-only flag / compliance review.
Jamal R.: Question: how do we surface the reasoning for automatic keeps? e.g., alerts and PII heuristics may bump a request into unredacted queue for analysis. We should show the rule id and a short human-friendly reason (max 80 chars).
Alex K.: Agreed — add `last_keep_reason` (string) and `keep_rule_id` to the UI. These are low-sensitivity metadata strings. No payload.
Sasha T.: Audit requirements: every time an export is approved we must append an immutable audit entry with actor, time, route, ticket id, ephemeral token id, TTL. Also retention policy: exports metadata kept 7 years, content only 180 days.
Priya M.: Ops question: will the console be calling the same API that the runtime uses for sampling decisions? we should avoid coupling. Suggest the console reads sampling config from config-store (read-only) and reads aggregated counters from telemetry service.
Jamal R.: Yes, console -> config-store + telemetry-agg. Export flow talks to export-service which calls runtime-admin to pull raw artifacts (with an admin-level role).
Alex K.: Small UX ask: add a per-route toggle for "show sampling breakdown" (default off) that teams can enable if they want more visibility. We should also add a global org-level setting to opt-out for privacy-first orgs.
Sasha T.: One more: rate-limiting on export requests (1 per 24h per org) and require a human reviewer in the approval path for first 30 days after rollout.
Priya M.: I'll update the privacy checklist and the design doc. Can someone note the follow-ups? 1) Add keep_reason doc; 2) Export approval flow RFC; 3) Console UI mockups with anonymized examples.
Jamal R.: I'll take (2) and (3). Alex — can you own (1)?
Alex K.: Yep, will draft keep_reason spec.
OpsBot: export-service v2 canary health: all checks pass.
Alex K.: Thank you — leaving this open for a few more comments then I'll create the RFC ticket.
